protocol.title: World-to-Digital-Microfluidic Interface Enabling Extraction and Purification of RNA from Human Whole Blood
protocol.platform: World-to-DMF (macroscale Extraction Module + DMF-based Purification Module, peristaltic pump driven)
protocol.sample_type: Human whole blood (fingerstick capillary range: 25, 50, or 100 uL)
protocol.objective: Inline concentration and recovery of RNA-bound magnetic beads from macroscale blood lysate via a 10 uL Bridging Droplet on a DMF device, followed by microscale wash/elution purification and downstream qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq analysis

system_modules: Extraction Module: two 500 uL microcentrifuge tubes (Reaction Chamber + Waste Chamber), peristaltic pump, Connector Tubes, Transfer Tubes
Purification Module: DMF device, 40 chromium electrode pads (6x6 mm, 40 um interelectrode gaps), Parylene-C dielectric (7 um), Teflon-AF (50 nm), 300 um air gap
Module Interface: Bridging Droplet (10 uL) formed on the Bridging Electrode at the periphery of the DMF device

reagents.filler_fluid: Fluorinert FC-40 (Sigma Chemical, St. Louis MO)
reagents.surfactant_additive: Pluronic F127, 0.1% w/v (added to Elution Buffer; Sigma Chemical)
reagents.lysis_solution: MagMAX-Blood lysis buffer (Life Technologies, Grand Island NY); 130 uL for 50 uL blood
reagents.rna_binding_beads: MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads, 20 uL (MagMAX-Blood RNA Isolation Kit, Life Technologies)
reagents.elution_buffer: MagMAX Elution Buffer + 0.1% w/v Pluronic F127, 10 uL on-device
reagents.dielectric_coating: Parylene C dimer (Specialty Coating Systems, Indianapolis IN)
reagents.whole_blood: Human whole blood from healthy volunteer donors (ProMedDx, Norton MA)

conventional_wash_volumes_uL.note: 12-fold reagent reduction vs. conventional method (15 uL vs 150-300 uL washes)

steps.name: Device initialisation
steps.notes: FC-40 filler fluid mixed with Pluronic F127 surfactant to prime DMF air gap. Purification Module reservoirs preloaded: Wash 1 (15 uL), Wash 2 (15 uL), Elution Buffer (10 uL + 0.1% Pluronic F127). Magnetic stand adjusted so Transfer Tubes contact Bridging Electrode at ~70 degrees. AC 100 Vrms actuation ready.

steps.name: Blood specimen introduction
steps.notes: 50 uL whole blood pipetted directly into Reaction Chamber (500 uL microcentrifuge tube). Specimens from healthy volunteer donors (ProMedDx, Norton MA).

steps.name: Lysis and mixing
steps.mechanism: peristaltic pump shuttles bolus between Transfer Tube 1 and Reaction Chamber
steps.notes: MagMAX-Blood lysis buffer aspirated from Transfer Tube 1 into Reaction Chamber and actively mixed with blood specimen for 30 s. Blood lysate formed.

steps.name: RNA Binding Bead addition and incubation
steps.notes: MagMAX silica-coated magnetic beads aspirated from Transfer Tube 1 into Reaction Chamber. Mixed 30 s, then incubated 5 min at RT to allow bead-RNA binding. Total reaction volume = 200 uL (50 + 130 + 20 uL).

steps.name: World-to-DMF transition: Bridging Droplet formation and bead capture (3 passes)
steps.operation: mix (x3) + heat (x3) [abstraction of pressure-driven convective flow-through]
steps.mechanism: Peristaltic pump drives full lysate volume through the 10 uL Bridging Droplet on the Bridging Electrode (Transfer Tube 1 -> Bridging Droplet -> Transfer Tube 2) while external magnet beneath Bridging Electrode immobilises RNA-bound beads. Repeated 3x for maximum bead recovery. Supernatant sent to Waste Chamber.
steps.transport: Pressure-driven convective transport (vs. diffusion-only in conventional method); accounts for slightly higher RNA capture at 100 uL blood volume
steps.bioscript_abstraction: `mix` abstracts convective flow-through; `heat at 25c` abstracts magnet engagement/disengagement (no native magnet instruction in BioScript)
steps.stale_variable_note: bridgingDroplet1/2/3 each consumed as input to successor mix; beadCapture is a fresh handle for the bead pellet remaining on the electrode surface after dispose of supernatant

steps.name: Wash 1
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (magnet re-engage) + dispose
steps.notes: Wash 1 Solution (15 uL) actuated onto Bridging Electrode by electrowetting. Magnet disengaged to release beads; bolus shuttled via Bridging Droplet for thorough washing. Magnet re-engaged; wash fluid sent to Waste Chamber. wash1Beads carries bead pellet to Wash 2.

steps.name: Wash 2
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (magnet re-engage) + dispose
steps.notes: Wash 2 removes residual chaotropic salts and ethanol from Wash 1. Identical bead-release/re-immobilise sequence. wash2Beads carries bead pellet to Elution.

steps.name: Elution
steps.operation: heat (magnet disengage) + mix + heat (incubation) + heat (magnet re-engage)
steps.eluate_collection: RNA-containing eluate driven to recovery site within Purification Module; collected by pipetting for off-device analysis
steps.notes: Elution Buffer (10 uL + 0.1% Pluronic F127) actuated onto Bridging Electrode. Beads resuspended; RNA released into eluate. Beads re-immobilised; eluate collected. Total processing time ~20 min (vs. 45 min conventional).

steps.name: RNA yield QC
steps.method: NanoDrop 2000 UV-vis spectrophotometry (A260) or Qubit 2.0 fluorometry (off-device)

pass.note: elutionMix NOT disposed here; must stay live for purity detect in BB4

fail.note: compiler emits dispose for both branches regardless of drain keyword

results.note: World-to-DMF gives slightly better yield at 100 uL blood (p=0.03); comparable at 25 and 50 uL

steps.name: RNA purity and integrity QC
methods: RNA integrity number (RIN): 2100 Bioanalyzer with RNA 6000 Pico Chip (off-device)
Fragment size distribution: Bioanalyzer; 28S and 18S rRNA peaks confirmed

qRT_PCR.template: 50 uL blood total RNA; SuperScript III cDNA; TaqMan/SsoFast Probes Supermix
qRT_PCR.result: Ct values essentially identical vs. conventional (p >= 0.07); no statistically significant difference

RNA_Seq.library_prep: Peregrine cDNA library + HAC molecular normalisation (rRNA depletion)
RNA_Seq.mapping: ~99% reads mapped to hg19 (UCSC) via TopHat v2.0.9
RNA_Seq.similarity: R^2 ~0.85 (Log10 FPKM) vs. conventionally prepared RNA; no strong bias

fail.note: compiler emits dispose regardless; both branches identical in IR

performance_comparison.rna_yield: comparable (p >= 0.16 at 25 and 50 uL; slightly better at 100 uL, p=0.03)
performance_comparison.rna_purity_A260_A280: comparable; all preparations high quality (Table S-1)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: device init; lysis; bead binding; 3-pass world-to-DMF bead capture; Wash 1; Wash 2; Elution; yield detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: purity detect on elutionMix (still live); puritySignal gate

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 7 basic blocks (BB1-BB7), 2 if/else gates, 8 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in seconds (s); no h token used

bugs_fixed.description: Stale variable reuse: wash1Mix, wash2Mix, and elutionMix re-read already-consumed bridgingDroplet2[0] and bridgingDroplet1[0]
bugs_fixed.fix: Introduced beadCapture (after dispose of bridgingDroplet3), then wash1Beads and wash2Beads as a linear chain through wash and elution steps. Each variable consumed exactly once.

bugs_fixed.description: Phantom variable elutionMix2[0]: elutionMix disposed inside BB2/BB3 yield branches, then re-read in BB4 purity detect. Compiler invented unreachable SSA version elutionMix2.
bugs_fixed.fix: Removed dispose(elutionMix) from yield if/else. Only yieldSignal disposed in BB2/BB3. elutionMix kept live into BB4.

bugs_fixed.description: drain keyword not emitted by compiler; IR always produces dispose. False branches used drain in source causing source/IR mismatch.
bugs_fixed.fix: Replaced all drain with dispose in both yield and purity QC else branches. Source now matches IR exactly.
